short: Setting prices to read cheaper than they are.
seoTitle: Psychological Pricing — Meaning and Example for Businesses
metaDescription: Psychological pricing sets prices at figures that read cheaper than they are — ₹199 instead of ₹200, or dropping the currency symbol on a menu.
definition: Psychological pricing sets prices at figures that read cheaper than they are — ₹199 instead of ₹200, or dropping the currency symbol on a menu. It works on how price is perceived rather than on what it costs.
bodyHtml:
Why Psychological Pricing matters

The technique is nearly free and measurably effective in consumer settings, and it also shapes comparison: an expensive item placed next to a mid-priced one makes the latter look reasonable.

How Psychological Pricing works in practice

Use charm endings in retail and casual dining, and round numbers in premium settings where value signals matter more. Menu design compounds the effect through position and the absence of a currency column.

faq.question: Does ₹199 really sell better than ₹200?
faq.answer: In consumer contexts it generally does. In premium and B2B settings it can cheapen the offer.

faq.question: Should menus show the rupee symbol?
faq.answer: Many restaurants drop it deliberately, since removing the currency cue softens price comparison.
